routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.added: 2026-09-03 (u-d4c), after the measurements above were pinned
routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.statement: the routing rows above were measured on FRESH scenarios carrying no published building edits, and they remain exact for every such scenario. Once a scenario has PUBLISHED a building edit, the executor accumulates the massing fold (PlanExecutor._applied_massing_edits, u-d4c) and EVERY later batch of ANY family routes through the building regeneration chain full tile with the full fold — the baseline-bound ExactWorker path would silently revert the published buildings (pre-existing engine defect since the u-c5/u-c6 chain seam, exposed user-facing by the u-d4 universal transport, fixed by the fold)
routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.effective_rule: building fold non-empty -> regeneration chain (full tile); fold empty (no published building edit since scenario creation/reset) -> the measured per-family routing rows apply unchanged
routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.cost_consequence: a post-building batch in a family that measured windowed/local above (e.g. vegetation ~56 s local, landcover ~local) instead pays the chain's cost class (building_dsm quiet totals 227.7-273.4 s, p50 241.6 s) until the scenario resets; correctness-mandated, not hidden
routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.diagnostics: chain-routed batches disclose routing in the executed plan's diagnostics: building_batch true, building_fold_size <int>, chain_carries_new_edits <bool> (false when the batch itself added no building edit but the accumulated fold routed it)
routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.fold_semantics: per-building-id last-write-wins vs the baseline anchor; deletes stay deletes (a deleted baseline building keeps before=baseline spec, after=null; a deleted session-added building keeps a tombstone anchored at the deleted session spec); the fold persists in scenario-state schema v3 and rides executor restarts
routing_disclosure_post_building_edit.overlap_order_disclosure: added 2026-09-03 (u-d4c remediation F1), after the measurements above were pinned: the fold applies to the chain in dict FIRST-INSERTION order (each building id's position is fixed by its FIRST appearance in the session, not by the session order of its latest edit), and the rasterizer replays that tuple sequentially — a delete's before-footprint reset is UNCONDITIONAL (it erases bystander paint at overlaps) while after-paints combine by fmax (taller wins). Overlapping DISTINCT building ids therefore resolve by application order and can diverge from a session-order sequential replay: add A (footprint FA), add B (FB overlapping FA), delete A folds to [A_tombstone(reset FA), B(paint FB)] and keeps B INTACT at FA∩FB, whereas a sequential replay [A, B, A_delete] would TRUNCATE B there (its reset lands last); deleting the LATER-inserted id instead ([A, B_tombstone]) truncates A at the overlap in BOTH orderings, so the divergence is asymmetric. It is bounded to the overlap cells of distinct building ids (the adapter carries no building inventory, so per-id last-write-wins cannot express cross-id occlusion; the fold semantics is unchanged and remains the mission-endorsed choice — this entry is a disclosure, not a behavior change)

anomalies.title: parallel-agent pytest pollution waves
anomalies.detail: two sibling agents (u-d0-residuals, u-d1-capability) ran pytest suites on this same machine throughout the sweep; load1 spiked from a ~5-8 baseline to 11-36 and foreign processes hit 141-312% CPU mid-run. Response per coordinator protocol: quiet gate before every run, mid-run load1/foreign tracking in the final pass, non-quiet runs kept in the record but excluded from stats, and families topped up until 5 quiet_valid runs existed. Runs discarded from final stats for load: {'vegetation': 3, 'meteorology': 8, 'landcover': 2, 'building_dsm': 9, 'model_parameters': 9, 'mixed_batch': 5}.

anomalies.title: code-state drift mid-sweep (two-phase protocol)
anomalies.detail: dispatch pinned 68e612f but the shared checkout advanced and carried uncommitted intermediate states during the first pass (hot-file mtimes 18:38-20:35), so first-pass families measured different code. Final pass re-measured everything at one fingerprint-pinned state (see code_state). Quiet p50 moved between passes: vegetation ~61.2 -> ~57 s, landcover ~42.6 -> ~38.3 s, meteorology ~156-161 -> ~140 s, model_parameters ~142-172 -> ~140 s, mixed ~145-167 -> ~140 s. Direction is consistently faster at the pinned state; attribution between the solver scratch-staging optimization and run-to-run variance is not separable from this data — reported as observed.

anomalies.title: loaded building runs measured FASTER than quiet runs
anomalies.detail: building_dsm runs 9-10 started behind a passing quiet gate but foreign waves arrived mid-run (load1 10.5/13.7); they measured 222.2 s and 230.4 s — faster than every quiet_valid building run (241.6-273.4 s). Plausible mechanism: higher ambient load keeps CPU clusters boosted instead of idling down between solver bursts. Consequence: the reported quiet-only stats are the CONSERVATIVE numbers for this family.

anomalies.title: building_dsm upward drift across sequential runs
anomalies.detail: quiet-gated building runs climbed monotonically within the first sweep (241.6, 255.9, 276.2, 283.1, 288.3 s) while RSS stayed flat (~1140 MB) and later runs under load came in lower again; even the clean pool spans 241.6-273.4 s (~13%). Not diagnosed further (read-only mandate); spread is reported in the stats.

anomalies.title: sampler thread death in building run 7 (fixed)
anomalies.detail: the RSS/load sampler thread died at its first foreign-busy tick (KeyError indexing a dict as tuple) so run 7 has 0 RSS samples; the run was excluded from stats anyway by the load_after=17.8 invalidation. Harness fixed for all later runs; no source code was touched.

anomalies.title: solver internal print inflates under contention
anomalies.detail: solver.py's own 'Time taken to execute tile 0_0' print reported 573.5 s during a first-pass run the external perf_counter span timed at 194.1 s (thread-time accumulation under load). All latencies in this file are external perf_counter spans; the worker's elapsed_seconds diagnostic agrees with them to ~1 ms.

anomalies.title: first-pass landcover 93.7 s outlier
anomalies.detail: the original 93.7 s landcover reading that triggered the load protocol was taken during a sibling pytest wave; quiet landcover runs measure 38.2-38.6 s at the pinned state. The outlier is retained in the archived first-pass record.

anomalies.title: PERF-002 reference is borderline
anomalies.detail: vegetation p95 at the pinned state is near the 60 s tree-local budget (P8 measured 59.14 s on the same machine class); see the family block for the exact value. Reported as reference, not forced.

UEDIT-008.statement: all six edit families carry >= 5 quiet-machine runs at one pinned code state with p50/p95/min/max/mean latency (executor.execute submit -> ExecutedPlan published), scientific-solve wall time split out of total, executor-local vs executor-full routing with the planner's reason, and peak RSS per run (psutil sampler, documented method)

UEDIT-007.statement: a view-only batch (output_view / OutputSelectionDelta, utci -> tmrt) driven through the full planner/executor path returns ExecutedPlan(status='no-op') BEFORE any staging or dispatch: zero worker job submissions, zero job ids minted, zero solve_window/run_full_tile calls, zero store publishes, zero patches, scene_revision unchanged at 0, plan node_impacts empty and estimated_work_units 0; the executor's own diagnostic reason is 'zero scientific stages (view-only or coalesced no-op batch): nothing to execute'. Control: a view edit riding a vegetation batch leaves job counts identical to the vegetation-only runs (1 worker.run, 1 job id, 1 store publish).
